Longitudinal Summary

Over the periods from Q1 2021 through Q4 2022, the company's current assets showed fluctuations primarily influenced by changes in cash and cash equivalents, accounts receivable, and inventory levels. There was a consistent pattern of increasing inventory to support production ramp-ups at various factories, partially offset by increases in accounts payable and accrued liabilities. Digital asset purchases and sales were a notable factor affecting cash flows but did not directly alter current assets classification. The company also recorded a full valuation allowance on net U.S. deferred tax assets by the end of 2021 and maintained it through 2022, indicating expectations of non-realization. Overall, current assets movements reflected operational scaling and strategic asset management rather than explicit forward guidance or forecasting.

Forecasting Credibility: None

No guidance versus actual pairs were provided for current assets, which is typical for mechanical or accounting line items that are not subject to forward-looking management forecasts. Therefore, it is not possible to assess management's forecasting credibility on current assets based on the available data. Any commentary or observed trends cannot substitute for direct guidance-actual comparisons in forming a credibility judgment.

Trends

  • Increasing inventory levels over time
  • Rising accounts payable and accrued liabilities
  • Stable or fluctuating cash and cash equivalents
  • Full valuation allowance on deferred tax assets from 2021 onward
  • Significant digital asset transactions impacting cash flows

Recurring Themes / Risks

  • Production ramp-up driving inventory increases
  • Accounts payable growth offsetting asset increases
  • Digital asset investments and related cash flow volatility
  • Deferred tax asset valuation uncertainty

Key Concerns

  • The full valuation allowance on U.S. deferred tax assets suggests management expects these assets will not be realized, which could impact future liquidity or tax planning.
  • Significant digital asset purchases and sales create cash flow variability but do not clearly affect current assets classification, potentially complicating liquidity assessments.
  • No forward guidance on current assets limits transparency and forecasting reliability for this balance sheet component.

Conclusion

Current assets have generally increased due to inventory buildup supporting factory production ramp-ups, partially offset by increases in accounts payable and accrued liabilities. Cash and cash equivalents have fluctuated but remained a significant component of current assets. The company’s digital asset transactions have influenced cash flows but are not directly reflected in current assets. The full valuation allowance on deferred tax assets indicates caution regarding asset realizability. Without forward guidance, management’s ability to forecast current assets cannot be evaluated, but the reported figures suggest current assets are managed in line with operational scaling and liquidity needs.

  • jump to section"The decrease in our net operating assets and liabilities was mainly driven by an increase in accounts payable and accrued liabilities in the three months ended March 31, 2021 as compared to a decrease in the three months ended March 31, 2020 from ramp up in production at Gigafactory Shanghai and the Fremont Factory and a smaller increase in inventory from buildup of finished goods from limited capacity to deliver or install our products at the end of the first quarter of 2020."
  • jump to section"This increase was primarily due to the decrease in net operating assets and liabilities of $1.44 billion and the increase in net income excluding non-cash expenses and gains of $747 million, partially offset by $101 million of net gain on digital assets."
  • jump to section"Accordingly, we believe that our current sources of funds will provide us with adequate liquidity during the 12-month period following March 31, 2021, including to pay down near-term debt obligations, as well as in the long-term."
  • jump to section"We have assessed the impact and are not aware of any specific events or circumstances that required an update to our estimates and assumptions or materially affected the carrying value of our assets or liabilities as of the date of issuance of this Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q."

  • jump to section"We currently account for all digital assets held as a result of these transactions as indefinite-lived intangible assets in accordance with ASC 350, Intangibles—Goodwill and Other ."
  • jump to section"Net investment in sales-type leases, which is the sum of the present value of the future contractual lease payments, is presented on the consolidated balance sheet as a component of Prepaid expenses and other current assets for the current portion and as Other assets for the long-term portion."
  • jump to section"We record restricted cash as other assets in the consolidated balance sheets and determine current or non-current classification based on the expected duration of the restriction."
  • jump to section"Accordingly, our interest rate swaps are recorded at fair value on the consolidated balance sheets within Other non-current assets or Other long-term liabilities, with any changes in their fair values recognized as Other income (expense), net, in the consolidated statements of operations and with any cash flows recognized as operating activities in the consolidated statements of cash flows."
  • jump to section"Our interest rate swaps were classified within Level II of the fair value hierarchy because they were valued using alternative pricing sources or models that utilized market observable inputs, including current and forward interest rates."
  • jump to section"As the terms of the arrangement convey a finance lease under ASC 842, Leases, we account for their production equipment as leased assets when production commences."
  • jump to section"Completed assets are transferred to their respective asset classes, and depreciation begins when an asset is ready for its intended use."
  • jump to section"Interest on outstanding debt is capitalized during periods of significant capital asset construction and amortized over the useful lives of the related assets."
  • jump to section"Depreciation on Panasonic production equipment is computed using the units-of-production method whereby capitalized costs are amortized over the total estimated productive life of the respective assets."
  • jump to section"As we now expect to settle a portion of the 2024 Notes in the second quarter of 2021, we reclassified $ 51 million of the carrying value of the 2024 Notes from debt and finance leases, net of current portion to current portion of debt and finance leases on our consolidated balance sheet as of March 31, 2021."
  • jump to section"Non-recourse debt refers to debt that is recourse to only assets of our subsidiaries."
  • jump to section"Recourse debt refers to debt that is recourse to our general assets."
  • jump to section"Securities Litigation Relating to Production of Model 3 Vehicles On October 10, 2017, a purported stockholder class action was filed in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California against Tesla, two of its current officers and a former officer."
  • jump to section"Litigation Related to Directors’ Compensation On June 17, 2020, a purported Tesla stockholder filed a derivative action in the Delaware Court of Chancery, purportedly on behalf of Tesla, against certain of Tesla’s current and former directors regarding compensation awards granted to Tesla’s directors, other than Elon Musk, between 2017 and 2020."
  • jump to section"The current dates for the trial are from July 12 to July 23, 2021, subject to change based on any further safety measures implemented by the Court."

Risk Factors
  • jump to section"In January 2021, we updated our investment policy to provide us with more flexibility to further diversify and maximize returns on our cash that is not required to maintain adequate operating liquidity, allowing us to invest a portion of such cash in certain alternative reserve assets including digital assets, gold bullion, gold exchange-traded funds and other assets as specified in the future."
  • jump to section"49 The prices of digital assets have been in the past and may continue to be highly volatile, including as a result of various associated risks and uncertainties."
  • jump to section"Moreover, digital assets are currently considered indefinite-lived intangible assets under applicable accounting rules, meaning that any decrease in their fair values below our carrying values for such assets at any time subsequent to their acquisition will require us to recognize impairment charges, whereas we may make no upward revisions for any market price increases until a sale, which may adversely affect our operating results in any period in which such impairment occurs."
  • jump to section"Finally, as intangible assets without centralized issuers or governing bodies, digital assets have been, and may in the future be, subject to security breaches, cyberattacks or other malicious activities, as well as human errors or computer malfunctions that may result in the loss or destruction of private keys needed to access such assets."
  • jump to section"For example, the prevalence of such assets is a relatively recent trend, and their long-term adoption by investors, consumers and businesses is unpredictable."
  • jump to section"Finally, the extent to which securities laws or other regulations apply or may apply in the future to such assets is unclear and may change in the future."

Risk Factors
  • jump to section"In January 2021, we updated our investment policy to provide us with more flexibility to further diversify and maximize returns on our cash that is not required to maintain adequate operating liquidity, allowing us to invest a portion of such cash in certain alternative reserve assets including digital assets, gold bullion, gold exchange-traded funds and other assets as specified in the future."
  • jump to section"53 We hold and may acquire digital assets that may be subject to volatile market prices, impairment and unique risks of loss."
  • jump to section"Moreover, digital assets are currently considered indefinite-lived intangible assets under applicable accounting rules, meaning that any decrease in their fair values below our carrying values for such assets at any time subsequent to their acquisition will require us to recognize impairment charges, whereas we may make no upward revisions for any market price increases until a sale, which may adversely affect our operating results in any period in which such impairment occurs."
  • jump to section"Finally, as intangible assets without centralized issuers or governing bodies, digital assets have been, and may in the future be, subject to security breaches, cyberattacks or other malicious activities, as well as human errors or computer malfunctions that may result in the loss or destruction of private keys needed to access such assets."
  • jump to section"For example, the prevalence of such assets is a relatively recent trend, and their long-term adoption by investors, consumers and businesses is unpredictable."
  • jump to section"Finally, the extent to which securities laws or other regulations apply or may apply in the future to such assets is unclear and may change in the future."

  • jump to section"We may need or want to raise additional funds through the issuance of equity, equity-related or debt securities or through obtaining credit from financial institutions to fund, together with our principal sources of liquidity, the costs of developing and manufacturing our current or future products, to pay any significant unplanned or accelerated expenses or 48 for new significant strategic investments, or to refinance our significant consolidated indebtedness, even if not required to do so by the terms of such indebtedness."
  • jump to section"46 Further, the implementation, maintenance, segregation and improvement of these systems require significant management time, support and cost, and there are inherent risks associated with developing, improving and expanding our core systems as well as implementing new systems and updating current systems, including disruptions to the related areas of business operation."
  • jump to section"Moreover, digital assets are currently considered indefinite-lived intangible assets under applicable accounting rules, meaning that any decrease in their fair values below our carrying values for such assets at any time subsequent to their acquisition will require us to recognize impairment charges, whereas we may make no upward revisions for any market price increases until a sale, which may adversely affect our operating results in any period in which such impairment occurs."
  • jump to section"Finally, as intangible assets without centralized issuers or governing bodies, digital assets have been, and may in the future be, subject to security breaches, cyberattacks or other malicious activities, as well as human errors or computer malfunctions that may result in the loss or destruction of private keys needed to access such assets."
  • jump to section"For example, the prevalence of such assets is a relatively recent trend, and their long-term adoption by investors, consumers and businesses is unpredictable."

  • jump to section"As of September 30, 2022 and December 31, 2021 , we had $ 671 million and $ 627 million, respectively, of long-term government rebates receivable in Other non-current assets on our consolidated balance sheets."
  • jump to section"Net investment in sales-type leases, which is the sum of the present value of the future contractual lease payments, is presented on the consolidated balance sheets as a component of Prepaid expenses and other current assets for the current portion and as Other non-current assets for the long-term portion."
  • jump to section"During the nine months ended September 30, 2022, we recorded $ 170 million of impairment losses on such digital assets, and $ 51 million and $ 101 million during the three and nine months ended September 30, 2021, respectively."
  • jump to section"As of September 30, 2022 and December 31, 2021 , the carrying value of our digital assets held was $ 218 million and $ 1.26 billion , which reflects cumulative impairments of $ 169 million and $ 101 million, each period, respectively."
  • jump to section"The fair market value of such digital assets held as of September 30, 2022 was $ 226 million."
  • jump to section"During the nine months ended September 30, 2022 and 2021, we purchased and/or received an immaterial amount and $ 1.50 billion, respectively, of digital assets."
  • jump to section"During the nine months ended September 30, 2022 and 2021, we realized gains of $ 64 million and $ 128 million, respectively, in connection with converting our holdings of digital assets into fiat currency."
  • jump to section"Accordingly, our interest rate swaps were recorded at fair value on the consolidated balance sheets within Other non-current assets or Other long-term liabilities, with any changes in their fair values recognized as Other (expense) income, net, in the consolidated statements of operations and with any cash flows recognized as operating activities in the consolidated statements of cash flows."
  • jump to section"Our interest rate swaps were classified within Level II of the fair value hierarchy because they were valued using alternative pricing sources or models that utilized market observable inputs, including current and forward interest rates."
  • jump to section"As the terms of the arrangement convey a finance lease under ASC 842, Leases , we account for their production equipment as leased assets when production commences."
  • jump to section"Completed assets are transferred to their respective asset classes and depreciation begins when an asset is ready for its intended use."
  • jump to section"Interest on outstanding debt is capitalized during periods of significant capital asset construction and amortized over the useful lives of the related assets."
  • jump to section"Depreciation on Panasonic production equipment is computed using the units-of-production method whereby capitalized costs are amortized over the total estimated productive life of the respective assets."
  • jump to section"Non-recourse debt refers to debt that is recourse to only assets of our subsidiaries."
  • jump to section"Recourse debt refers to debt that is recourse to our general assets."
  • jump to section"On June 16, 2022, two Tesla stockholders filed separate derivative actions in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Texas, purportedly on behalf of Tesla, against certain of Tesla’s current and former directors."
  • jump to section"Litigation Related to Directors’ Compensation On June 17, 2020, a purported Tesla stockholder filed a derivative action in the Delaware Court of Chancery, purportedly on behalf of Tesla, against certain of Tesla’s current and former directors regarding compensation awards granted to Tesla’s directors, other than Elon Musk, between 2017 and 2020."
  • jump to section"We expect to meet the capital expenditure and tax revenue requirements based on our current level of spend and sales."

Risk Factors
  • jump to section"In January 2021, we updated our investment policy to provide us with more flexibility to further diversify and maximize returns on our cash that is not required to maintain adequate operating liquidity, allowing us to invest a portion of such cash in certain alternative reserve assets including digital assets, gold bullion, gold exchange-traded funds and other assets as specified in the future."
  • jump to section"Moreover, digital assets are currently considered indefinite-lived intangible assets under applicable accounting rules, meaning that any decrease in their fair values below our carrying values for such assets at any time subsequent to their acquisition will require us to recognize impairment charges, whereas we may make no upward revisions for any market price increases until a sale, which may adversely affect our operating results in any period in which such impairment occurs."
  • jump to section"Finally, as intangible assets without centralized issuers or governing bodies, digital assets have been, and may in the future be, subject to security breaches, cyberattacks or other malicious activities, as well as human errors or computer malfunctions that may result in the loss or destruction of private keys needed to access such assets."
  • jump to section"For example, the prevalence of such assets is a relatively recent trend, and their long-term adoption by investors, consumers and businesses is unpredictable."
  • jump to section"Finally, the extent to which securities laws or other regulations apply or may apply in the future to such assets is unclear and may change in the future."
  • jump to section"The prices of digital assets have been in the past and may continue to be highly volatile, including as a result of various associated risks and uncertainties."

MD&A
  • jump to section"The increase in our net operating assets and liabilities was mainly driven by a larger increase of inventory in the year ended December 31, 2022 as compared to the year ended December 31, 2021, partially offset by a larger increase of accounts payable and accrued liabilities, to support the ramp up in production at our factories and larger increases in other non-current assets and prepaid expenses and other current assets."
  • jump to section"As of December 31, 2022, we had recorded a full valuation allowance on our net U.S. deferred tax assets because we expect that it is more likely than not that our U.S. deferred tax assets will not be realized."
  • jump to section"Additionally, cash inflows related to sales of digital assets were $936 million in the year ended December 31, 2022, and net cash outflows related to digital assets were $1.23 billion in the year ended December 31, 2021 from purchases of digital assets for $1.50 billion offset by proceeds from sales of digital assets of $272 million."
  • jump to section"During the years ended December 31, 2022 and 2021, we also realized gains of $64 million and $128 million, respectively, in connection with converting our holdings of digital assets into fiat currency."
  • jump to section"Accordingly, we believe that our current sources of funds will provide us with adequate liquidity during the 12-month period following December 31, 2022, as well as in the long-term."

  • jump to section"We may need or want to raise additional funds through the issuance of equity, equity-related or debt securities or through obtaining credit from financial institutions to fund, together with our principal sources of liquidity, the costs of developing and manufacturing our current or future products, to pay any significant unplanned or accelerated expenses or for new significant strategic investments, or to refinance our significant consolidated indebtedness, even if not required to do so by the terms of such indebtedness."
